S3 Cross-Region Replication Tampering [Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-306] on Primary S3 Bucket, Secondary S3 Bucket, S3 Replication Configuration, KMS Keys: Attackers could modify replication rules, exploit KMS key permissions, or tamper with replication role permissions to disrupt the replication process or access replicated data. Backup Process Denial of Service [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on AWS Backup, Storage Gateway, S3 Buckets, EC2 Instances, Aurora Clusters: Attackers could initiate numerous concurrent backup jobs, consume S3 API limits, or overwhelm Storage Gateway resources to prevent successful backup completion. An attacker exploits the lack of rate limiting on backup requests to initiate thousands of concurrent backup jobs, exhausting AWS Backup service quotas and preventing legitimate backups.

Unauthorized Access to Archived Data [Information Disclosure, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-284] on Primary S3 Bucket, Secondary S3 Bucket, S3 Glacier Storage, IAM Roles: Attackers could exploit overly permissive IAM policies or S3 bucket policies that don't properly restrict access to archived data, potentially accessing sensitive historical data. An attacker discovers an IAM role with broad S3 permissions that allows them to initiate Glacier retrievals and access archived sensitive data.

Backup Data Integrity Compromise [Tampering, Repudiation, CWE-367] on Storage Gateway, AWS Backup, S3 Buckets, Aurora Clusters, DynamoDB Tables: Attackers could exploit timing vulnerabilities in backup processes or race conditions in concurrent backup operations to corrupt or modify backup data. During a large backup operation, an attacker exploits a race condition to modify data being written to S3, resulting in corrupted or incomplete backups.

Cross-Region Data Exfiltration [Information Disclosure, CWE-319] on Primary S3 Bucket, Secondary S3 Bucket, Aurora Global Database, DynamoDB Global Tables: Attackers could exploit misconfigured cross-region permissions or weak encryption settings to access and exfiltrate data across regions. An attacker compromises a secondary region role to access encrypted data, then exploits weak KMS key policies to decrypt and exfiltrate sensitive information.
